title: Character
body:
`char`. One character, one byte. An [[Atomic type]]. Literals use single quotes: `'a'`.
Double quotes make a string, which is a different thing entirely.

```c++
char grade = 'A';
char next = grade + 1;    // 'B', because a char is a small integer
```

A `char` *is* a number. `'A'` is 65, `'a'` is 97, `'0'` is 48, so `digit - '0'` converts a
character digit to its value. The mapping is [[ASCII]], covered properly in
[[COMPUTING MACHINERY]].

An [[Array]] of `char` terminated by `'\0'` is a [[C-String]].
